source: TMUA 2018 · Paper 1 · Question 19 · Official worked answer

hints.title: Draw both triangles on the same ray
hints.body: Fix A and B, then draw the ray from A making the given angle with AB. The two possible positions of C lie on this ray and are each the given distance from B.
hints.recap: An SSA specification can allow two different triangles.
hints.pitfall: Draw both positions using the same fixed side and angle.
hints.pause: Label the shorter unknown side from A by a variable and mark the common perpendicular height from B.

recall.reminder: An SSA specification can allow two different triangles.

hints.title: Use the area ratio before the side rule
hints.body: Taking the two collinear unknown sides as bases gives the same perpendicular height for both triangles. Convert the given area ratio into a ratio of those side lengths.
hints.recap: Triangles with the same perpendicular height have areas proportional to their bases.
hints.pitfall: These two triangles are not generally similar, so do not square the side ratio.
hints.pause: Express the longer side in terms of the shorter one, then write the cosine rule for both triangles.

recall.reminder: Triangles with the same perpendicular height have areas proportional to their bases.

hints.title: Eliminate the shared terms
hints.body: Subtract your two cosine-rule equations. The known squared sides cancel, leaving a relation between the shorter side and the cosine of the fixed angle.
hints.recap: Subtracting equations can remove a shared geometric quantity.
hints.pitfall: Only divide by a side length after using the fact that it is positive.
hints.pause: Substitute your relation back into either equation and select the geometrically allowed sign of the cosine.

recall.reminder: Subtracting equations can remove a shared geometric quantity.

solution:
1. Relate the two unknown sides. Let the shorter AC length be t>0. Both triangles have the same height from B to the ray AC, so the longer length is 3t.

2. Apply the cosine rule twice. With u=cosθ, 49=t2+100−20tu and 49=9t2+100−60tu. Subtracting gives 0=8t2−40tu. Since t>0, t=5u, which also shows u>0.

3. Substitute and check the sign. The first equation becomes 49=25u2+100−100u2, giving u2=17/25. Positivity gives cosθ=175. The side lengths are 17 and 317; both form nondegenerate triangles with sides 7 and 10. Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Relate two SSA triangles by equal-height areas and eliminate their cosine-rule equations
